Hi Priya — thanks for sending this over and for the time yesterday.

We can absolutely provide concise, auditor-ready answers. I'm attaching a one-page summary (PDF) plus a data flow diagram. High-level answers up front:

- Residency: Hosted API storage is in the US by default; we can restrict tenant data to US regions only for enterprise accounts on request.
- Retention: Customer request payloads are stored for 30 days by default; embeddings and derived artifacts are retained for 90 days by default. Both windows are configurable on enterprise plans (down to 0 days / immediate deletion) or up to 365 days for audit purposes.
- Deletion: We support immediate erasure on request via console or API, with deletion propagated to primary stores within 24 hours and to backups within 30 days. We provide a deletion certificate (hash + timestamp) for audit.
- Telemetry: Operational telemetry and anonymized metrics are retained for 180 days; raw request logs used for debugging are automatically redacted and retained no longer than 90 days unless opt-in.

I'll loop Ben (Sales engineering) and Aditya (Security/engineering) to add the technical nuances and provide the CSV matrix you requested for inclusion in your risk tool.

Ben / Kim — draft below for the questionnaire section. Please review; I kept it short for insertion into the one-page PDF.

-- DRAFT ANSWERS --
1) Classification: Derived artifacts such as embeddings and vectors generated by the Hosted API are treated as customer data for the purposes of retention and erasure requests. Customers can opt to disable storage of derived artifacts; when disabled, embeddings are not written to persistent store and are only used in-memory for the request lifecycle.

2) Primary stores and backups:
- Primary: request payloads, embeddings, and associated metadata are stored in encrypted object stores (AES-256) within the customer's configured region (US by default).
- Backups / snapshots: automated daily snapshots are taken for recovery. Snapshots are write-once within the backup system and cannot be modified, but they are subject to retention policies and are purged according to the deletion lifecycle below.

3) Deletion mechanics and timeline:
- Immediate erasure request processed within 24 hours to remove primary-store objects and metadata indices.
- Snapshot/backup purge scheduled within 30 days; for legal holds or enterprise custom SLAs this window can be shortened via a support ticket and contractual amendment.
- Proof of deletion: we issue a deletion certificate that includes object identifiers, a SHA256 hash of removed records, timestamp, and the operator ID.

4) Operational telemetry: logs that contain PII are redacted at ingestion. Aggregated telemetry retained for 180 days; raw debug logs retained no longer than 90 days by default.

Notes: If Helios needs a stricter backup purge (e.g., 7 days), we can scope that in an addendum and implement a faster snapshot lifecycle.

--END DRAFT--

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the concise answers to questions 12-18 (PDF) and a CSV retention matrix that maps object classes to default and configurable windows. Key points summarized below for your reviewers:

- Residency: Hosted API tenant data is stored in US regions by default. For enterprise customers we support region-restriction to US-only (no cross-region replication) — please indicate this requirement in your order form.

- Embeddings & derived artifacts: Treated as customer data. Embeddings are retained by default for 90 days; customers can opt-out of persistent storage or configure a shorter retention window (minimum immediate deletion).

- Deletion & backups: We execute deletion from primary stores within 24 hours of an erasure request. Backups/snapshots are purged within 30 days; if Helios requires an accelerated snapshot purge (e.g., 7 or 14 days) we can include that in the contract and operationalize via a shortened retention lifecycle. We provide a deletion certificate (SHA256 fingerprint + timestamp + operator ID) for audit evidence.

- Telemetry: PII is redacted at ingestion. Aggregated metrics retained 180 days; raw debug logs 90 days by default.
